DONE — full run on the approved design. Headline = **M2 (total effect)**, reference = White. Language associative throughout; every number tagged with its model.

## 0. Execution & validity checks (before any results)
- `analysis/lib_fit.py`: own Newton–Raphson logit + **Firth penalized logit** (penalized likelihood ℓ+½log|XᵀWX|; Fisher scoring on U* = Xᵀ(y−μ)+½Xᵀ[h(1−2μ)]). Validated 3 ways: (a) matches statsmodels MLE to **5e-16** (β, se, loglik); (b) intercept-only Firth = analytic Jeffreys (s+0.5)/(N+1) to **1e-9**; (c) stays finite (β=16.3) where MLE diverges (β=1479) on separated toy data. A first version had a leverage bug (used I instead of I⁻¹) — caught by check (b), fixed.
- Bootstrap: 2,000 case resamples, 0 discarded. Delta-method and bootstrap CIs agree (Black-vs-White interaction: delta 1.757 [1.214, 2.543] vs bootstrap ratio-of-RRs 1.750 [1.206, 2.490]).
- matplotlib cannot be installed offline → figure emitted as a hand-built **SVG** (parses cleanly; 9 polylines, 3 bootstrap bands, 15 empirical points) plus CSV grids.

## 1. Headline coefficient table (M2 = `logit P(BA) ~ z(SES)*C(race, ref=White) + male`; 1 SD SES = 0.742 raw units)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| **SES × Black** | 0.5638 | 0.1886 | **1.757** | 1.214–2.543 | 0.0028 (Holm 0.0056) |

| male | −0.2295 | 0.1333 | 0.795 | 0.612–1.032 | 0.085 |
logLik −1051.37 (7 params). SES main effect in M0/M1a: OR 1.30/SD; ignoring race (M1b): 1.42.

**Interaction tests:** 2-df LRT for race × SES (M1a→M2) **χ²(2)=9.63, p=0.0081**; per-term Wald + Holm over the 2 contrasts: Black 0.0056, Hispanic 0.110.
**Relevelled runs (Black, Hispanic references)** reproduce identical magnitudes with signs flipped (ref=Black: zses_x_White = −0.5638 → same 1.757 Black/White ratio), and the reference-invariant contrast matrix gives Black-vs-White 1.757 [1.214, 2.543] Holm p=0.0084; Hispanic-vs-White 1.409 [0.925, 2.147] Holm p=0.220; Hispanic-vs-Black 0.802 [0.477, 1.350] p=0.406 → **no claim rests on the reference level.** Race-stratified logits (M4) agree with the joint model: 1.176 / 2.067 / 1.642 vs 1.176 / 2.067 / 1.658.

**Difference-in-RD (your additive-scale question):** RD Black−White **+0.43 pp [−0.24, +1.08]** boot p=0.24; RD Hispanic−White +0.31 pp [−0.52, +1.14] p=0.48; RD Hispanic−Black −0.12 pp [−0.96, +0.76] p=0.76. Ratio-of-RRs Black/White **1.75 [1.21, 2.49]** p=0.004; Hispanic/White 1.41 [0.92, 2.08] p=0.11.
→ **Modification survives on the multiplicative scale, not on the absolute scale** — expected, not contradictory: baselines are ~2.6× lower (1.31% Black, 1.67% Hispanic vs 3.37% White at mean SES), so even a doubling of odds moves absolute risk <1 pp. Warning: the ratio-of-**RD** statistics in the CSV are numerically unstable (RD_White ≈0.5 pp is a near-zero denominator; bootstrap SD up to 65) and are labelled UNSTABLE — read difference-in-RD and ratio-of-RRs instead.

## 3. Functional form (your specific concern) — linearity NOT rejected
| test (all nested in M2 / vs M2) | χ² | df | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| shared z(SES)² | 0.138 | 1 | 0.711 |
| z(SES)² × race | 0.482 | 3 | 0.923 |
| RCS(4 knots: z=−1.53/−0.41/0.28/1.80) × race vs linear × race | 8.810 | 6 | 0.185 |
| shared RCS nonlinearity given linear × race | 4.722 | 2 | 0.094 |
| modification under flexible shape (linear+RCS×race vs RCS×race) | 4.088 | 4 | 0.394 |
(First spline attempt with patsy `cr()` produced a singular design with |β|≈300 — replaced by a hand-built Harrell RCS basis, after which fits converged normally.)
The "White flat Q2→Q4" hint is **not** supported as nonlinearity: within-race quintile rates are White 2.34/4.32/3.37/3.76/3.93%, Black 0.24/0.71/1.89/1.42/2.37%, Hispanic 0.75/0.38/1.13/1.89/3.03% — White's Q3–Q4 dip is within overlapping CIs. Per your ruling I still report race-specific slopes + fixed-point predicted probabilities; the per-SD summary is defensible. Crude top/bottom within-race quintile rate ratios: White 1.68, Hispanic 4.02, Black 10.02 → the modification is not a modelling artefact.

| M2 z(SES) | 0.1623 (0.0745) | 0.1636 (0.0742) | 1.176 | 1.178 |

Probability scale: diffRD Black−White 0.0043 (MLE) vs 0.0046 (Firth). **No material difference** (<2% on the log-odds scale, CIs never flip a verdict); all models converged, no separation → MLE retained as headline.

## 6. M3 sensitivity — in full, labelled as conditioning on likely SES-path variables
M3 = M2 + z(ABILITY) + z(PERCENTILE) (logLik −908.40; LRT vs M2 χ²(2)=285.9; ability OR/SD 2.77, percentile OR/SD 1.71). VIFs < 3 (ability 2.65, percentile 2.08; r=0.699) → interaction not unstable, it is interpretable.
Race-specific OR per SD SES — M2: White 1.176 / Black 2.067 / Hispanic 1.658; **M3: White 0.759 [0.642,0.898] / Black 1.336 [0.922,1.936] / Hispanic 0.980 [0.655,1.467]**; ability-only (M3a) 0.758/1.272/0.962; percentile-only (M3b) 0.884/1.746/1.228.
Key pattern: **the interaction does not shrink** — ratio of ORs Black/White 1.757 (M2) vs 1.760 (M3), 1.679 (M3a), 1.975 (M3b); Hispanic/White 1.409 → 1.291. What collapses is the **within-White** SES gradient (1.18 → 0.76). Reported as mechanism evidence per your ruling: measured ASVAB ability and class percentile absorb most of the SES→completion association among White respondents, while a residual positive gradient persists in the Black group (only group with positive M3 slope). M3 never overwrites M2 in the hypothesis.

## 7. HYPOTHESIS (DiscoveryBench payload)
**Among NLS respondents, the association between socioeconomic status and completing a BA degree runs along racial lines: the SES gradient in degree completion is steepest for Black respondents, intermediate for Hispanic respondents, and flattest for White respondents.** In the total-effect logistic model (BA ~ z(SES) × SAMPLE_RACE + SAMPLE_SEX, reference White; N = 8,773; 236 completions = 2.69%), the adjusted odds of completing a BA per 1 SD (0.742 raw units) of SES were 2.07 (95% CI 1.47–2.90) for Black respondents and 1.66 (1.12–2.46) for Hispanic respondents, versus 1.18 (1.02–1.36) for White respondents — a significant race × SES interaction (2-df LRT χ² = 9.63, p = 0.008), driven by the Black contrast (interaction OR 1.76, 1.21–2.54, Holm p = 0.008); the Hispanic contrast points the same way but is not detectable at this precision (1.41, 0.93–2.15, Holm p = 0.22; 19 events). The divergence concentrates at higher SES: predicted completion rises from 0.45% at −1.5 SD to 5.4% at +2 SD for Black respondents versus 2.7% to 4.6% for White respondents, and at mean SES Black and Hispanic respondents still have ~2.6× lower completion chances (1.31%, 1.67% vs 3.37%). The modification is therefore clear on relative measures (RR of completion for +0.5 SD vs −0.5 SD SES: 2.05 Black, 1.64 Hispanic, 1.17 White; Black/White ratio 1.75, 1.21–2.49) but not on absolute ones (difference-in-RD Black−White 0.43 pp, 95% CI −0.24 to +1.08); for the Hispanic contrast and the additive scale generally there is **no detectable modification given this precision**, which is not evidence of absence. The pattern is not attributable to functional form (quadratic p = 0.71; spline-by-race p = 0.18), reference category, estimator (Firth shifts estimates <2%), or adjustment strategy: adding ASVAB ability and class percentile — a direct-effect-flavoured sensitivity conditioning on plausible SES-path variables — leaves the Black-vs-White interaction essentially unchanged (1.76 in both) while collapsing the within-White SES gradient from 1.18 to 0.76, suggesting the measured achievement variables absorb much of the SES-completion association for White respondents but not the steeper gradient seen for Black respondents. All statements are associative; no causal claim is supported.

## 8. Limitations
Thin high-SES cells (Black 34, Hispanic 26 respondents within ±0.2 SD at z=+1.5) bound the reliability of dotted curve tails; 19/28 minority events give wide CIs, so the Hispanic contrast and all additive-scale contrasts are under-powered; no survey weights/strata, single cohort; test-score and curriculum columns described in datasets.json are absent from the file (residual confounding by school quality unaddressable); "higher percentile = better" remains an **inferred** coding assumption (r = +0.70 with ASVAB, graded with SES) — if inverted only the M3/M3b reading changes, not M2 or the headline; ability/percentile as mediators bar causal reading of M3; "racial lines" refers only to the three sample race categories.

The divergence is concentrated at higher SES: predicted completion rose from 0.45% at SES -1.5 SD to 5.4% at +2 SD for Black respondents versus 2.7% to 4.6% for White respondents, and at mean SES Black and Hispanic respondents still had about 2.6x lower completion chances (1.31% and 1.67% vs 3.37%). payload.workflow: 1) Inspection of data/nls_ses_processed.csv (N=8,773 rows = 8,773 unique CASE IDs, one row per respondent, zero missing values, no duplicates or sentinel codes; outcome BA DEGREE COMPLETED stored as boolean, 236 True = 2.69%). 2) Preprocessing: outcome coerced to 0/1; SES, ASVAB ability composite and class percentile standardized on the full sample (SDs 0.7423 / 345.74 / 25.579); race dummy-coded with White as reference; sex dummy-coded; no rows dropped. 3) Models (custom Newton-Raphson logistic fitter validated against statsmodels to 5e-16): M0 unadjusted, M1a main effects with race, M1b without race, M2 PRIMARY total-effect interaction model logit P(BA) ~ z(SES)*race + male, M3 sensitivity adding z(ability) + z(percentile) plus ability-only and percentile-only variants, M4 race-stratified logits, M2 relevelled with Black and Hispanic references, and a robust-Poisson supplementary. 4) Interaction inference: 2-df likelihood-ratio test for the race x SES block (chi2=9.63, p=0.0081), per-term Wald tests with Holm adjustment across the two contrasts, delta-method race-specific SES slopes and pairwise interaction contrasts computed from the joint covariance (reference-invariant, cross-checked against relevelled fits). 5) Marginal effects: g-computed predicted P(BA) per race at fixed SES levels; RD and RR for +0.5 SD vs -0.5 SD and +/-1 SD, plus difference-in-RD and ratio-of-RRs, with 2,000-resample case-bootstrap percentile CIs cross-checked against the delta method. 6) Functional form: quadratic and quadratic-by-race likelihood-ratio tests plus a Harrell restricted cubic spline (4 knots at the 5/35/65/95 percentiles) by-race test; linearity retained (all p >= 0.09). 7) Sparse-data sensitivity: Firth penalized-likelihood fits (penalty 0.5*log|X'WX|) of the joint model and each race-stratified model, reported alongside the raw MLE numbers; implementation validated against the analytic intercept-only Jeffreys estimate and against divergence behaviour under separation. 8) Diagnostics: VIFs for M2 and M3 (max 2.65), predictor correlation matrix, model-free completion rates by within-race SES quintile, and local cell counts around each SES grid point. 9) Outputs: predicted-probability curves clipped to each race's observed SES range (solid within the central 96% of that race's range, dotted in sparse regions, 95% bootstrap bands, overlaid model-free quintile rates and thin-cell counts) as results/figure_predicted_prob_by_race.svg; all tables as CSVs; results/report.md assembled programmatically from those CSVs.
